principles: Keep Quantum implementation claim-bounded and local-only.
Fail closed on stale, missing, mismatched, or unbound evidence.
Reuse the existing proof-admissibility vocabulary and binding style instead of creating a second proof system.
Ship the smallest useful runtime slice before verifier adapters, gates, and benchmarks.
drivers: Quantum plan delivery axis says M0-M1 must precede M2-M5.
The user wants execution, but not overclaiming scientific truth or runtime completeness.
Existing Proofbound code runtime already has proof-admissibility primitives that should anchor this work.

options.name: narrow-m0-m1-evaluator
pros: Delivers schema and deterministic identity binding now.
Keeps M2-M5 pending exactly as the plan requires.
Allows focused smoke coverage without introducing a premature plugin framework.
cons: Does not yet provide verifier adapters, lifecycle gate integration, or benchmark rates.
Future stories must still formalize a generic adapter-pack framework if desired.

options.name: full-quantum-pack-now
pros: Would appear to execute more of the written plan in one story.
Could include verifier adapters, gate policy, and benchmark output sooner.
cons: Too broad for one story and likely to blur design contract with delivered runtime.
Risks unsupported scientific or benchmark claims before M1-M3 are verified.

options.name: generic-framework-first
pros: Creates a reusable ClaimAdmissibilityPack abstraction before Quantum-specific code.
Could reduce duplication across PINN and Quantum later.
cons: Delays the concrete Quantum M0-M1 slice the user asked to execute.
Risks inventing abstraction before the second runtime pack proves exact common seams.

rationale: Choose the narrow M0-M1 evaluator because it executes the Quantum plan in the order the document requires, creates concrete runtime value, and avoids overclaiming M2-M5 or scientific correctness.

preMortem.scenario: The implementation accidentally claims Quantum runtime completeness.
preMortem.trigger: Docs, smoke output, or result structures say M2-M5, benchmark, or verifier adapters are delivered.
preMortem.consequence: Users may believe Proofbound can validate quantum simulations end-to-end when only M0-M1 exists.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep status wording explicit: M0-M1 only; M2-M5 pending; no benchmark execution before M1-M3.

preMortem.scenario: Identity binding over-blocks valid deterministic tasks.
preMortem.trigger: The schema requires randomSeed or timeStepHash for static deterministic claims that do not use them.
preMortem.consequence: False stops make the domain pack look unusable for normal eigenvalue or figure provenance checks.
preMortem.mitigation: Implement core required fields and claim-specific conditional identity fields exactly as the Quantum plan describes.

preMortem.scenario: Weak evidence is upgraded into a strong quantum claim.
preMortem.trigger: Single-run energy evidence is accepted for a stronger ground-state or convergence claim.
preMortem.consequence: The pack violates Proof-or-Stop claim-boundary semantics.
preMortem.mitigation: Add smoke cases proving weak evidence degrades or stops rather than advancing stronger claims.

preMortem.scenario: The story duplicates the generic adapter-pack framework work.
preMortem.trigger: New interfaces or registries are introduced broadly under core proof-admissibility.
preMortem.consequence: The narrow Quantum story collides with the separate framework document and increases review surface.
preMortem.mitigation: Implement only Quantum-specific primitives under a bounded module; leave generic framework formalization to a separate story.
